issues.description: CHANGELOG entry filename does not match the actual check directory/name
issues.detail: CHANGELOG.md adds `compute_instance_single_network_interface` but the PR title and description say `compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces`. The on-disk check is named `compute_instance_single_network_interface`. Verify the intended name and align PR title/description, or the changelog will reference the wrong check.

issues.description: GKE detection by name prefix is unreliable and trivially spoofable
issues.detail: Using `instance.name.startswith("gke-")` to classify GKE-managed nodes lets any attacker or operator bypass the check by naming a multi-NIC VM `gke-foo`. GCE labels (`goog-gke-node`) or instance metadata are the documented, reliable signals. This silently downgrades real findings to MANUAL.

issues.description: Metadata and check behavior disagree about GKE/MANUAL handling
issues.detail: metadata.json describes only PASS/FAIL outcomes and the Risk/Description make no mention of MANUAL, but the check emits a MANUAL status for GKE instances. Update the metadata Description/Notes (and any docs) to document the MANUAL outcome so users/scanners understand the third state.

issues.description: Zero-network-interface branch emits PASS with no test coverage
issues.detail: When `interface_count == 0` the code falls through with the initial `status = "PASS"` and a status_extended saying "has no network interfaces." That semantically conflicts with PASS ("single network interface") and is untested. Either set status to INFO/MANUAL or add an explicit test; current behavior is misleading in reports.

issues.description: NetworkInterface name may be empty, producing confusing status_extended
issues.detail: `compute_service._get_instances` defaults `name` to `""` when the API omits it. The check then prints `"has a single network interface: ."` or comma-joins empty strings. Consider falling back to a synthetic label like `nic{index}` or filtering blanks before joining.

issues.description: Test `test_compute_no_instances` asserts zero findings but never sets project_ids
issues.detail: Unlike the other tests, this one omits `compute_client.project_ids`. It currently passes because the check loops over `instances`, but if a future report constructor requires `project_ids` this silently breaks. Set `project_ids` for consistency with the rest of the suite.

review.summary: The check is straightforward but the PR has a naming inconsistency that will land in the public changelog: title and description say `compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces`, while disk artifacts and CHANGELOG say `compute_instance_single_network_interface`. The GKE carve-out uses an unreliable name-prefix heuristic that an attacker can trivially bypass, and the MANUAL outcome is not described in metadata.json. The zero-interface branch reports PASS, which is semantically wrong for a "single network interface" check and is untested. Other issues are minor (empty NIC names, missing project_ids in one test).
